name: MOPS-Hub for Beginners (MH4B)
description: The High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider requires a scalable and reliable detector-control infrastructure for the ATLAS Inner Tracker. A central part of this infrastructure is the readout of the Monitoring Of Pixel System (MOPS) chips, which monitor local voltages and temperatures through a radiation-tolerant Controller Area Network (CAN)-based interface and expose the resulting telemetry through Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) to the supervisory control system. Before the Embedded Monitoring and Control Interface–Embedded Monitoring Processor (EMCI–EMP) production chain can be qualified, the communication chain must be tested under reproducible laboratory conditions and with enough observability to distinguish physical bus behavior, tester-side logging effects, middleware readback, and value-consistency deviations. This thesis develops and evaluates a deterministic Hardware-in-the-Loop validation infrastructure for the ATLAS Inner Tracker Detector Control System MOPS readout chain. The work combines custom readout hardware, STM32 firmware, OPC UA middleware integration, Windows Control Center Open Architecture (WinCC OA) visualization, and a Python-based validation logger into one measurement and analysis workflow.
